## SEM Effects

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
::: {.fragment}
- Direct effect: X > Y
  - Unstandardized: For every 1-SD increase in X, Y changes by the b standard deviations. 
  - Standardized: For every 1-SD increase in X, Y changes by b standard deviations 
:::
:::

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
::: {.fragment}
- Indirect effect: X > M > Y: Multiply path coefficients to get indirect effects
  - Unstandardized: For every 1-unit increase in X, Y changes by the product's units, because X changed M, which then changed Y.
  - Standardized: For every 1-SD increase in X, Y changes by the product's standard deviations, because X changed M, which then changed Y.
:::
:::

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
::: {.fragment}
- Total effect: Direct + indirect effects
:::
:::

Note that not all models have direct effects/total effects

## Model Interpretation

![Reading scores example - unstandardized](images/mvpa.png)
 
## Interpretation: 

a * b = indirect effect

0.15 * 30.65 = 4.597

- Unstandardized: For every 1-unit increase in X (parent Ed), Y (reading score) changes by 4.597 units (points).

# Standardized Interpretation

0.272 * 0.424 = .115

- Standardized: For every 1-SD increase in X (parent Ed), Y (reading score) changes by .115 standard deviations.

## Standardized vs Unstandaridized

- Unstandaridized: 
  - often easier to interpret raw units (i.e. points)
  - needed for replication

- Standardized: 
  - Shows effect size of variables on different scales (i.e. parent ed vs points relative importance)
